title: European Declaration on Quantum Technologies
executive_summary: The European Declaration on Quantum Technologies underscores the strategic significance of quantum technologies for the EU’s scientific and industrial competitiveness. Signed by twenty-six Member States, the declaration commits these countries to collaborate in building a world-class quantum technology ecosystem across Europe. The ultimate goal is to establish Europe as the global leader in quantum excellence and innovation, positioning it as the ‘quantum valley’ of the world. This collective effort aims to drive advancements in quantum technologies, ensuring Europe’s leadership in this critical field.
characteristics: Recognises the strategic importance of quantum technologies for the EU’s scientific and industrial competitiveness.
Commits signatory Member States to collaborate on developing a world-class quantum technology ecosystem across Europe.
Aims to make Europe the global leader (“quantum valley”) in quantum excellence and innovation.
As of May 2025, twenty-six EU Member States have signed the declaration.
practical_applications: Twenty-six EU Member States have signed the European Declaration on Quantum Technologies, establishing a formal multilateral commitment to collaborate on developing a world-class quantum technology ecosystem across Europe.

top_actors.name: EU Member States
top_actors.justification: The EU Member States are the direct signatories of the Declaration, explicitly listed and central to the commitment and implementation of the quantum technologies initiative. Their collaboration and decisions are the driving force behind the document's objectives.

top_actors.name: European Union
top_actors.justification: The European Union provides the overarching framework, strategic direction, and legitimacy for the Declaration. The initiative is positioned as an EU-wide effort, and the EU is responsible for shaping Europe's digital future, as referenced in the document.

top_actors.name: Governments
top_actors.justification: Governments are implicitly involved as the representatives of the Member States and are responsible for enacting the commitments made in the Declaration. However, they are less directly mentioned and specified than the Member States and the EU itself.

top_themes.name: Quantum Technologies
top_themes.justification: Quantum technologies are the explicit and central focus of the declaration, which recognizes their strategic importance for the EU's scientific and industrial competitiveness. The entire document is dedicated to advancing quantum technologies and building a world-class ecosystem in this field.

top_themes.name: Digital & Technological Partnerships
top_themes.justification: The declaration emphasizes collaboration among EU Member States to develop a unified quantum technology ecosystem. This theme is crucial for achieving the document's objectives, as it underpins the commitment to joint action and shared innovation across Europe.

top_themes.name: Multilateralism
top_themes.justification: The document highlights the multilateral nature of the agreement, with 26 EU Member States as signatories. While this is important for legitimacy and scale, it is slightly less central than the direct focus on quantum technologies and the mechanisms of partnership.
